title: Sprint traffic thermometer and shift microledger
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact working doc for the June sprint release focused on traffic-aware canarying. The goal: provide an hourly traffic "thermometer" (a simple heuristic gauge) + a microledger for shift handoffs (who saw what and when), with clear telemetry ownership and a minimal set of release notes to publish after stabilization. This is intentionally concise and operational — expect handwritten notes during the launch.

Summary / Context:
- Release target: 2026-06-18 18:00 UTC (3-hour window)
- Primary change: model-routing policy + autoscale tweak for dedicated pools, plus a small API surface fix (REL-4123).
- Risk profile: medium. Changes touch routing and autoscaling; latency risk in RU/EU regions.
- Quick win: staged canary with traffic thermostat and automatic rollback if latency or error thresholds breach.

Thermometer concept (simple):
- GREEN: 0–30% of target traffic routed to new variant; latency delta < +8% and error rate < 0.05% over 5m
- WARM: 31–60% routed; latency delta < +12% and error rate < 0.1% over 5m
- HOT: 61–90% routed; latency delta < +20% and error rate < 0.25% over 5m; manual attention required
- FAULT: any step where error rate > threshold OR sustained p50/p95 increases beyond defined buckets -> immediate rollback to previous model routing policy and notify PG

Operator microledger (live notes template):
- Each handoff: timestamp | operator | watch-zone (GREEN/WARM/HOT) | signal summary (errors/latency/traffic %) | action taken | notes
- Example row (copy during shift): 2026-06-18T18:12Z | Marco L | WARM | p95 +9%, 0.04% 5xx, 42% traffic | paused ramp, notified infra | saw a few node OOMs on pool-3

Preflight checklist (72h / 24h / 1h):
- 72h: validate canary config in staging; run full smoke suite; confirm artifact hashes; run traffic replay at 50% of expected load window; confirm canary abort hook exists in orchestration; confirm on-call roster for release day
- 24h: freeze non-essential deploys; snapshot routing configs; ensure alerting pages set (LatencyGate/CanaryAbort); run dry-run in prod-sim with synthetic 5k requests; ops slack channel created #release-thermometer
- 1h: scale target pools to baseline; warm caches/prefixes with representative prompts; ensure KV cache metrics surfaced; confirm operator microledger spreadsheet is shared and editable

Cutover cadence (hour-by-hour, launch + 3h watch):
- T0 (18:00 UTC): start canary at GREEN (20% traffic to new routing)
- T0+15m: evaluate metrics (p50, p95, 5xx rate, queue latency). If green -> move to WARM (50%); if borderline -> hold 15m; if fault -> rollback
- T0+45m: if WARM stable -> advance to HOT (80%); else hold/rollback
- T0+90m: if HOT stable -> complete rollout (100%) with gradual smoothing over 30m; otherwise keep at highest stable step and run mitigations
- T0+3h: begin stabilization digest and prepare release notes

Rollback decision criteria (quick):
- 5xx errors spike > 0.25% sustained over 5m at GREEN/WARM
- p95 latency increase > 20% sustained over 5m at any stage
- any resource OOM/crashloop observed in dedicated pool
- user-visible regression flagged by solutions engineering triage (SE must page ops lead)

Telemetry ownership (who watches what):
- Latency / p50/p95: Jordan Reeves (eng-observability) -> primary
- Error rates (4xx/5xx): Priya Desai (infra) -> primary
- Autoscale queueing/backpressure: Marco Lin (platform) -> primary
- End-to-end customer error surface (prod) / CS alerts: Anya Morales (customer-success) -> subscriber and will escalate
- Microledger updates + notes: Release operator on duty (rotate every 60–90 min) -> primary

Smoke + quick tests (to run during GREEN):
- 50 short prompt generation calls across variants (verify no decoding regressions)
- Embeddings sanity check for 10 long-form inputs (compare dim/mean)
- Session resume test for chat stateful flows (KV cache hit sanity)
- Auth + quota check for tokenized requests (ensure no regression on rate limit paths)

Release notes (draft template for post-stabilization):
- Title: June sprint: model-routing safety rollout + autoscale tuning
- Short blurb: Deployed a staged change to how requests are routed across model variants to improve p95 latency under increasing load. Includes an autoscaling buffer adjustment to reduce cold-start latency for dedicated pools.
- Impacted areas: hosted API routing, dedicated pools autoscale behavior, and small API bugfix (REL-4123)
- Rollout details: staged canary with automated thermostat-based progression; full rollout completed 2026-06-18 19:45 UTC (if successful)
- Rollback notes: Automatic rollback triggered if latency or error thresholds breached; none triggered OR list incidents if occurred
- Followups / known issues: concise list of degradations observed and mitigations planned

Post-release stabilization tasks (first 72h):
- 0–12h: maintain increased telemetry sampling for impacted routes; ops to run hourly checks and update microledger; capture any customer escalations
- 12–48h: run comparative traffic-cost analysis; run a long-tail latency sampling for 95/99th percentiles; engineering to assess if autoscale parameters can be tightened
- 48–72h: ship a brief postmortem if any rollback or significant incident occurred or a stabilization summary if the rollout was clean

Open questions / TODOs (rolling):
- Is the thermostat threshold for WARM p95 delta (+12%) too tight for RU region? Jordan to provide RU baseline by 2026-06-14
- Need a succinct blurb for the changelog that customer success can send (one paragraph). Anya + PR by 2026-06-17 AM
- Should we add a synthetic golden-check that runs automatically at each step? Pros/cons noted below.

Handy commands / links (scratch):
- Canary abort: /ops/release/abort REL-4123 (internal hook)
- Watch panels: dashboards.prod/redwood/release-thermometer (live)
- Microledger: drive/shared/releases/thermometer-microledger-2026 (shared sheet)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the microledger tiny; long tables get ignored in the middle of an incident. One line per operator + explicit action.
- If we see >1 node OOM in pool-3 within 30m, treat as a hard stop and rollback.
- Avoid immediate escalations for transient p95 blips under synthetic load; focus on user-facing error rates and sustained latency.

Appendix: quick watchlist (copy for shift briefing)
- p95 delta > 12% -> ring Jordan (obs)
- 5xx sustained > 0.1% at WARM -> ring Priya (infra)
- queue depth rising > 2x baseline -> ring Marco (platform)
- any customer CS page -> tag Anya and ops lead

-- end --

(If anything here is unclear or you'd like a condensed operator card that fits on one A4, say so and I'll draft a minimal one-page checklist.)
